analysis: What changed vs the 5:00 AM brief: the overnight story deepened rather than changed, and the morning's big scheduled print landed benign. Nasdaq 100 futures slipped to -2.52% (from -2.33%) while the Dow stayed flat, and the 8:30 a.m. ET Employment Cost Index came in exactly as expected (+0.8% q/q, decelerating from +0.9%), removing the hot-wage risk that could have turned a tech rotation into a market-wide selloff — Morningstar notes Treasury yields fell to just above 4.92% as investors trimmed December-hike expectations. The second fresh item, Binance's $6.34B cover for the $6.3B hack with $3B frozen, caps the crypto-exchange fear but leaves bitcoin near $77,356 after a $76,400 overnight low and $1.57B in liquidations. Signal: the market's grading rubric is now explicit across all three big-tech reports this week — cash conversion and guidance beat revenue growth. Alphabet (-$9.07B FCF), Amazon (-$42.4B TTM FCF) and even beat-and-raise Microsoft are all being read through that lens, and Intel's PC warning has turned a single-stock guide miss into a chip-and-PC sector repricing (AMD, Broadcom, Nvidia, SanDisk, Dell, HP all lower). Noise: Thursday's breadth held up (9 of 11 sectors green, advancers ahead, Russell +1.01%, equal-weight S&P +1.20%) and energy is offsetting, so this remains a concentrated megacap-tech de-risking, not broad risk-off — the open's test is whether that containment holds once Chicago PMI and Fed speakers land.
disclaimer: Not financial advice — for informational purposes only.

headlines.headline: Fresh this hour: Q3 Employment Cost Index rose 0.8% q/q, exactly as expected, after +0.9% in Q2 — wages +0.7% (vs +0.9% prior), benefits +0.9% (vs +1.0% prior), and +3.4% over 12 months, unchanged from the year through June.
headlines.why_it_matters: An in-line, decelerating wage print removes the morning's hot-inflation tail risk — it does not offset the tech earnings drag, but it keeps the December-hike debate from getting worse into the open.

headlines.headline: Futures deepen into the open: Nasdaq 100 futures -2.52%, S&P 500 futures -1.05%, Dow futures flat, as Amazon and Intel earnings extend Thursday's tech selloff; Amazon and Intel together are set to shed about $300 billion in market value if premarket losses hold.
headlines.why_it_matters: Still a concentrated tech open, not broad risk-off — the Dow flat while the Nasdaq sinks more than 2.5% shows the pressure is in AI-spending names, not the whole market.

headlines.headline: Amazon -7.42% premarket to $225.70 (Finnhub, 08:57 ET) after Q3 missed: net sales $201.9B vs ~$202.3B expected, EPS $1.89 vs ~$1.96-1.97 expected, despite AWS +39% to $46.0B; trailing-12-month free cash flow swung to -$42.4B from +$14.8B a year earlier, with 2026 cash capex held at ~$220B and 2027 capex set to rise further.
headlines.why_it_matters: Record AWS growth could not offset the cash line — the market is grading AI spenders on free cash flow, and Amazon just joined Alphabet on the wrong side of that test.

headlines.headline: Intel -25.72% premarket to $68.39 (Finnhub, 08:57 ET) despite a Q3 beat: revenue $16.5B (+21% y/y), adjusted EPS $0.52 vs ~$0.41 expected, data-center/AI +78% to $7.3B — but Q4 guidance of $15-16B revenue and $0.25 EPS trails the ~$17.1-17.3B / $0.43-0.45 consensus, with the PC market warned to decline into at least H1 2027.
headlines.why_it_matters: A demand warning from Intel hits the whole chip complex, not just one stock — see the spillover below.

headlines.headline: Chip and PC spillover widens: AMD -8.64%, Broadcom -3.79%, Nvidia -2.40% premarket to $208.53 (Finnhub, 08:57 ET), SanDisk down over 8% and SK Hynix over 7%; HP fell over 8% and Dell over 10% premarket on Intel's PC warning.
headlines.why_it_matters: Intel's guide is now a sector read — memory, chip and PC-hardware names are all being repriced on the same PC-demand and supply-constraint warning.

headlines.headline: Megacap premarket snapshot (Finnhub, 08:57 ET): Meta -1.68% to $614.03, Microsoft -0.29% to $528.58, Apple -0.95% to $345.59; Alphabet was only about -0.47% premarket per TipRanks after Thursday's 12.64% rout to $283.82, its worst day since its 2004 IPO.
headlines.why_it_matters: Even Thursday's relative winners are being pulled in — Microsoft's cash-backed beat is no longer an offset when the whole tech complex is de-risking, while Apple is holding up best among the megacaps.

headlines.headline: Fresh this hour: Binance set aside more than $6.34B in company resources to cover the $6.3B hack, with $3B in stolen assets frozen by partners; withdrawals remain paused pending security checks. Bitcoin fell to an overnight low near $76,400 before recovering to about $77,356, and crypto liquidations jumped to $1.57B.
headlines.why_it_matters: The cover announcement caps the immediate exchange-loss fear, but the hack still weighs on crypto sentiment — bitcoin is the session's separate risk-off leg, not a driver of equity futures.

headlines.headline: Energy is the morning's offset, carried forward: ExxonMobil and Chevron both beat Q3 profit expectations on a refining surge — Exxon adjusted EPS $4.23, Chevron $5.28, shares +2% and +1% premarket at the 5:00 AM check; WTI rose 2.1% to $104.13 and Brent's expiring December contract rose about 1.6% to near $117.70.
headlines.why_it_matters: Strong oil-major prints plus higher crude reinforce the rotation out of tech and help keep the Dow near flat while Nasdaq futures sink.

headlines.headline: Prior session (Thu Oct 29) hid a rotation: S&P 500 -0.30% to 7,720.39, Nasdaq -1.38% to 26,184.72, Dow -0.25% to 52,342.56 — but 9 of 11 sectors rose, advancers outnumbered decliners on both exchanges, the Russell 2000 gained 1.01% to 2,859.22, and the equal-weight S&P rose 1.20% while the cap-weighted index fell.
headlines.why_it_matters: The headline declines overstate Thursday's damage — breadth held up, so today's question is whether the Amazon/Intel leg finally breaks that rotation or stays contained in tech.

market_snapshot.breadth_notes: Prior regular session (Thu Oct 29): 9 of 11 S&P sectors rose; advancers outnumbered decliners on both exchanges; Russell 2000 +1.01%; equal-weight S&P +1.20% vs cap-weighted -0.30%. No S&P advance/decline ratio or volume-vs-average figure was shown in sourced pages for the Thu close. Premarket VIX around 18.5 per CAMS morning brief.
market_snapshot.notes: Fri Oct 30, 6:00 AM PT — 30 minutes before the 6:30 AM PT open. Futures per TradingKey premarket roundup (Dow flat, S&P -1.05%, Nasdaq -2.52%); VIX ~18.5 per CAMS; 10-year just above 4.92% per Morningstar/Dow Jones Newswires, -1 bp vs the 5:00 AM brief's 4.93%. WTI $104.13 (+2.1%) per AP; gold briefly below $4,000 per Morningstar; bitcoin ~$77,356 per CoinDesk, down more than 3% over 24 hours after an overnight low near $76,400.

usac.why_it_matters: No fresh USAC company news in this hour's sourced coverage. Q3 earnings land before the open Tue Nov 3 (11 a.m. ET call) and the $0.525 Q3 distribution ($2.10 annualized) pays Nov 6 to holders of record Oct 26. Last reported quarter (Q2, Aug 4): EPS $0.31 beat the $0.28 consensus, revenue $342.15M vs $340.49M expected. Oil rebounding premarket (WTI $104.13, +2.1%) and the Exxon/Chevron refining beats keep a supportive energy backdrop, with no company-specific catalyst ahead of Nov 3.

Monday Nov 2 after the close: Apple reports fiscal Q4 — the last megacap verdict on the AI-spending question.
USAC: Q3 earnings before the open Tue Nov 3; $0.525 distribution payable Nov 6. AMD also reports Nov 3.
